$comment: Agent notes for the platform: getting updates and webhooks, managed bots, games, Telegram Passport errors. Shape and rules: scripts/api_notes.py. Every pitfall carries its source label; API means the catalog text quoted in cite. Server setup (TLS, certificates, hosting) is out of scope.

getUpdates.purpose: Receive updates by long polling: ask Telegram for new updates and confirm them with offset.
use_when: development, one process, or a host without a public HTTPS URL
an agent process behind NAT
avoid_when: a webhook is set: getUpdates does not work until deleteWebhook

pitfalls.text: offset = highest update_id received + 1; an update is confirmed once getUpdates is called with a higher offset. Recalculate it after every response.
pitfalls.cite: offset: An update is considered confirmed as soon as getUpdates is called with an offset higher than its update_id.

pitfalls.text: timeout defaults to 0, short polling for tests only; pass a positive long-poll timeout.
pitfalls.cite: timeout: Defaults to 0, i.e. usual short polling. Should be positive, short polling should be used for testing purposes only.

pitfalls.text: allowed_updates is sticky: omitted keeps the previous list; an empty list means all types except chat_member, message_reaction, message_reaction_count.
pitfalls.cite: allowed_updates: If not specified, the previous setting will be used.

pitfalls.text: Incoming updates are kept on the server until received, at most 24 hours.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getting-updates

pitfalls.text: Save the offset after the batch is handled and make handlers idempotent.

setWebhook.purpose: Have Telegram POST every Update as JSON to your HTTPS URL instead of polling.
use_when: an always-on HTTPS service in production
several workers sharing the load (max_connections)
avoid_when: no public HTTPS URL: use getUpdates

pitfalls.text: secret_token (1-256 chars of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ and -) comes back in the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header of every request; check it to know the request is yours.
pitfalls.cite: secret_token: A secret token to be sent in a header ... in every webhook request, 1-256 characters. Only characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ and - are allowed.

pitfalls.text: A non-2XX answer makes Telegram repeat the request until it gives up after a reasonable number of attempts.
pitfalls.cite: setWebhook: In case of an unsuccessful request (a request with response HTTP status code different from 2XY), we will repeat the request and give up after a reasonable amount of attempts.

pitfalls.text: Updates can repeat or arrive out of order: dedupe and reorder by update_id.
pitfalls.cite: Update.update_id: allows you to ignore repeated updates or to restore the correct update sequence, should they get out of order

pitfalls.text: allowed_updates is sticky; ports 443, 80, 88 and 8443 only.
pitfalls.cite: allowed_updates: If not specified, the previous setting will be used.; Ports currently supported for webhooks: 443, 80, 88, 8443.

pitfalls.text: Answer 2XX fast and process from a queue; keep secret_token in the environment, never in code.
The number of retries and their timing are not stated.

deleteWebhook.purpose: Remove the webhook so the bot can receive updates with getUpdates again.
use_when: switching a bot from webhook to long polling
before close when moving between local Bot API servers
avoid_when: only the URL changes: call setWebhook with the new URL

pitfalls.text: drop_pending_updates: true drops all pending updates.
pitfalls.cite: drop_pending_updates: Pass True to drop all pending updates

pitfalls.text: Without it, pending updates stay on the server until received, at most 24 hours.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getting-updates

pitfalls.text: setWebhook with an empty url also removes the webhook.
pitfalls.cite: url: Use an empty string to remove webhook integration.

pitfalls.text: Drop pending updates only when losing them is intended, from the deploy step.

getWebhookInfo.purpose: Read the webhook status: URL, pending update count, last delivery error, allowed_updates.
use_when: the bot receives nothing: check it first
verifying after setWebhook

pitfalls.text: An empty url means the bot uses getUpdates.
pitfalls.cite: getWebhookInfo: If the bot is using getUpdates, will return an object with the url field empty.

pitfalls.text: last_error_date and last_error_message describe the latest delivery error; last_synchronization_error_date a Telegram-side sync error.
pitfalls.cite: WebhookInfo.last_error_message: Error message in human-readable format for the most recent error that happened when trying to deliver an update via webhook

pitfalls.text: secret_token is not returned and can't be read back.
pitfalls.cite: WebhookInfo fields: none for secret_token

pitfalls.text: Alert when pending_update_count keeps growing or last_error_date is recent.

getManagedBotToken.purpose: Fetch the token of a bot your bot manages, after the managed_bot update names it.
use_when: a managed_bot update or managed_bot_created message names a new bot
a managed_bot update says its token changed
avoid_when: per request: fetch once and keep it in a secret store

pitfalls.text: Returns the managed bot's token as a plain String.
pitfalls.cite: getManagedBotToken: Returns the token as String on success.

pitfalls.text: The token is a secret: never log, echo or send it to a chat or URL; keep it in a secret store.
user_id is the managed bot's id (ManagedBotUpdated.bot), not the user who created it.
pitfalls.cite: user_id: User identifier of the managed bot whose token will be returned

pitfalls.text: managed_bot also arrives when the token or owner changes: fetch it again then.
pitfalls.cite: Update.managed_bot: A new bot was created to be managed by the bot, or token or owner of a managed bot was changed

pitfalls.text: The error for a bot you no longer manage is not stated.

replaceManagedBotToken.purpose: Revoke a managed bot's current token and get a new one.
use_when: the managed bot's token leaked
a rotation the owner approved
avoid_when: an automatic retry: every call revokes the token in use

pitfalls.text: The current token is revoked; whatever still uses it must switch to the returned one.
pitfalls.cite: replaceManagedBotToken: revoke the current token of a managed bot and generate a new one. Returns the new token as String on success.

pitfalls.text: The new token is a secret: write it straight to the secret store, never log, echo or send it.
After a timeout, read the token with getManagedBotToken instead of replacing again.
Whether a managed_bot update follows a replacement the manager bot made itself is not stated.

getManagedBotAccessSettings.purpose: Read who may use a managed bot: everyone, or only its owner plus listed users.
use_when: showing the owner the current access before a change
verifying after setManagedBotAccessSettings

pitfalls.text: Returns BotAccessSettings; added_users lists the other users only when access is restricted.
pitfalls.cite: BotAccessSettings.added_users: The list of other users who have access to the bot if the access is restricted

pitfalls.text: The owner always has access.
pitfalls.cite: BotAccessSettings.is_access_restricted: The bot's owner can always access it.

setManagedBotAccessSettings.purpose: Restrict a managed bot to its owner plus up to 10 users, or open it to everyone.
use_when: the owner wants a private or team-only bot
keeping a bot private until launch
avoid_when: without the owner's decision: it changes who can use their bot

pitfalls.text: added_user_ids holds up to 10 users besides the owner and is ignored when is_access_restricted is false.
pitfalls.cite: added_user_ids: A JSON-serialized list of up to 10 identifiers of users ... Ignored if is_access_restricted is False.

pitfalls.text: Whether added_user_ids replaces or extends the current list is not stated: send the full list.

sendGame.purpose: Send an HTML5 game created in @BotFather (/newgame) as a message with a Play button.
use_when: a game registered in @BotFather with a game_short_name
a high-score table in the chat
avoid_when: channels and channel direct messages chats: not supported
a small in-chat board without @BotFather setup: a widget

pitfalls.text: Without reply_markup one 'Play game_title' button is shown; with a keyboard the first button must launch the game (callback_game).
pitfalls.cite: reply_markup: If empty, one 'Play game_title' button will be shown. If not empty, the first button must launch the game.

pitfalls.text: Play sends a CallbackQuery with game_short_name; answer with answerCallbackQuery url = the game URL for this user.
pitfalls.cite: answerCallbackQuery.url: If you have created a Game and accepted the conditions via @BotFather, specify the URL that opens your game

pitfalls.text: Put a signed session (user, chat, message) in the game URL so scores can't be forged.

setGameScore.purpose: Record a user's score in a game message; by default the message is edited to show the scoreboard.
use_when: your server accepted a finished round
avoid_when: a score the browser reports unchecked

pitfalls.text: Errors when the score is not above the current one unless force; force also lowers a score (mistakes, cheaters).
pitfalls.cite: setGameScore: Returns an error, if the new score is not greater than the user's current score in the chat and force is False.

pitfalls.text: Pass chat_id + message_id or inline_message_id; returns the Message, or True for an inline message.
pitfalls.cite: setGameScore: if the message is not an inline message, the Message is returned, otherwise True is returned.

pitfalls.text: disable_edit_message keeps the message text unchanged.
pitfalls.cite: disable_edit_message: Pass True if the game message should not be automatically edited to include the current scoreboard

pitfalls.text: The error code and text for a score that is not higher are not stated.

getGameHighScores.purpose: Read the high-score rows around a user in a game message.
use_when: a leaderboard screen inside the game
showing a user's rank after setGameScore
avoid_when: a complete ranking: keep your own table

pitfalls.text: Returns the user and two neighbours on each side, plus the top three if they are not among them; Telegram says this may change.
pitfalls.cite: getGameHighScores: This method will currently return scores for the target user, plus two of their closest neighbors on each side. ... Please note that this behavior is subject to change.

pitfalls.text: Returns an Array of GameHighScore (position, user, score), also for inline_message_id.
pitfalls.cite: getGameHighScores: Returns an Array of GameHighScore objects.

setPassportDataErrors.purpose: Tell a user which Telegram Passport elements they sent are wrong, so they fix and resend them.
use_when: a decrypted element fails your checks: invalid birth date, blurry scan, signs of tampering
avoid_when: data your service accepts: each flagged element blocks a resubmission until it changes

pitfalls.text: The user can't resubmit until every error is fixed: the flagged field or file must change.
pitfalls.cite: setPassportDataErrors: The user will not be able to re-submit their Passport to you until the errors are fixed (the contents of the field for which you returned the error must change).

pitfalls.text: Each error is a PassportElementError picked by source; unspecified takes element_hash = EncryptedPassportElement.hash.
pitfalls.cite: EncryptedPassportElement.hash: Base64-encoded element hash for using in PassportElementErrorUnspecified

pitfalls.text: data_hash and file_hash come from the decrypted DataCredentials and FileCredentials.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/passport

pitfalls.text: Say in message what to fix; never quote the user's document data in it.
